newsitem.title: CANADA: Skyjack Inc gets C$32 mln of new orders.
newsitem.headline: Skyjack Inc gets C$32 mln of new orders.

text.p: SkyJack Inc said it received about C$32 million worth of new orders as a result of its attendance at the American Rental Association show in New Orleans.
The company said these new orders bring its total order backlog to C$83 million, down marginally from the record C$92 million backlog at this time last year.

It said Skyjack has received strong orders for the new boom and scissor models, approximately 30 percent of the current order backlog will not be produced until after the end of the current fiscal year.

Due to this delay, a decline of approximately C$5 million of Skyjack's revenues for the fourth quarter is anticipated. As a result, the Company has taken steps to reduce expenses, including a reduction of the overall workforce by approximately four percent.
Skyjack is still experiencing strong sales in scissors and booms in Canada and Europe and new initiatives in the Pacific Rim are also generating new business opportunities.
The Company also anticipates an overall reduction in gross profit, estimated at 2.5 percent for both the fourth quarter and the next fiscal year.
It said the lower estimate is primarily as a result of flattening scissor sales and increasing boom sales, which currently have lower margins.

"Overall, we are expecting lower net earnings for the fourth quarter relative to both the prior year and the recently concluded third quarter, said Wolf Haessler, Skyjack President and chief executive officer.

"However, improvements are expected for the latter half of fiscal 1998 as many of our plans to enhance productivity, lower costs and accelerate new product introductions within the Skyjack's core product lines, will begin to be realized."
